skill.name: update-stock-mcp
skill.description: Configure, update, and query a compatible DuckDB database of A-share market data through MCP, with optional QuantAll integration.
skill.summary: Manage A-share DuckDB market data and QuantAll settings through MCP.
skill.author: mifochen

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, expected DuckDB operations, loopback URLs, fixed-path configuration writes, and hardcoded subprocess arguments. The source still has SQL injection, plaintext token storage, and unrestricted database-file creation. No prompt injection or obfuscated payload was found.

remediation.issue: Stock query parameters are interpolated directly into SQL.
remediation.suggestion: Use DuckDB parameter binding for values and validate symbols and dates with strict allowlists before every query.

remediation.issue: The Tushare API token is stored in a plaintext file.
remediation.suggestion: Read the token from a protected secret store or environment variable, and enforce restrictive file permissions when a file fallback is necessary.

remediation.issue: Creat_DB can create a database at any writable path.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve paths into an approved data directory, reject traversal and sensitive locations, require confirmation, and enforce a storage limit.

semantic_findings.title: SQL Injection in Stock Query Tools
semantic_findings.description: Both price-query tools concatenate symbol and date inputs directly into SQL. An untrusted MCP caller can alter queries and may access unintended data through DuckDB features.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The MCP parameters are inserted into executable SQL with f-strings and no validation or parameter binding. Both public query tools use the same vulnerable pattern.

semantic_findings.title: Plaintext API Token Storage
semantic_findings.description: Documentation requires placing the Tushare API token in API_tushare.txt, and update tools read it as unencrypted text. Any process or user with file access can recover it.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation and both update functions explicitly use a plaintext file for the credential. No encryption, secret store, or permission hardening is present.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted Database File Creation
semantic_findings.description: Creat_DB accepts an arbitrary path and DuckDB creates a new database without restricting the destination. A compromised agent can create files or consume storage wherever the process can write.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The public MCP tool passes its path argument to DuckDB after checking only that the target does not exist. There is no allowed-directory or storage-limit check.

content.user_title: Manage A-Share Stock Data in DuckDB
content.value_statement: Maintaining current A-share market data across several tables is slow and operationally complex. This skill configures, updates, and queries a compatible local DuckDB database through MCP tools.
actual_capabilities: Generate local settings and table mappings for a compatible seven-table DuckDB market database.
Run full Tushare updates or a lighter Tushare and Baostock update for price tables.
Query raw or forward-adjusted daily prices by stock symbol and date range.
Save the selected database path and QuantAll history window in local configuration.
Launch an installed QuantAll package as a local MCP service on port 8686.
Send progress notifications during long market data updates.
limitations: A Tushare token is required for Tushare updates, and the full workflow requires at least 2,000 Tushare points.
Initial full updates can take several hours and depend on external data provider availability.
Database creation is unreliable because initialization opens the new file before the seven-table schema is built.
The token uses a plaintext file, and queries use SQL interpolation, so only trusted local users and inputs are suitable.

prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether UpdateStock is connected. Then retrieve raw daily prices for {symbol} from {start_date} through {end_date} and summarize missing dates.

prompt_templates.prompt: Connect the existing compatible DuckDB database at {approved_path}. Save the path, verify required tables, and report any schema mismatch.

output_examples.output: The query returned daily open, high, low, close, previous close, volume, and turnover values ordered by trading date.

best_practices: Use a dedicated database directory, confirm every path, and back up valuable files before creation or updates.
Protect the Tushare token with restrictive permissions and never include it in prompts, logs, or source control.
Validate stock symbols and dates before queries, and review long updates or service launches before execution.
anti_patterns: Do not pass untrusted stock symbols or dates until the SQL queries use parameter binding.
Do not create databases in system directories, shared locations, or paths containing unrelated files.
Do not interrupt full updates without expecting partial data, and do not launch an unreviewed QuantAll installation.

faq.question: Can this version create a new database?
faq.answer: Creation is unreliable because initialization occurs before schema creation. Use a compatible existing DuckDB database until this is corrected.

faq.question: Is a Tushare token required?
faq.answer: Yes for Tushare updates. Baostock supplies part of the lighter workflow, but stock price updates still use Tushare.

faq.question: Which update mode should I use?
faq.answer: Use the full mode with at least 2,000 Tushare points. Use the lighter mode with approximately 120 to 200 points.

faq.question: Can it return adjusted prices?
faq.answer: Yes. It can return raw daily prices or calculate forward-adjusted prices for a symbol and date range.

faq.question: Does it modify local files?
faq.answer: Yes. It creates DuckDB files, writes local settings, reads a token file, and can generate a QuantAll launcher.

faq.question: What does QuantAll integration require?
faq.answer: It requires the separate QuantAll package, an approved DuckDB database, local port 8686, and acceptance of the QuantAll user agreement.
